findings.reason: it would have the author pin which provenance path supplies the synthesised keys' layer, removing a convention the implementer would otherwise invent and that a later project-layer override would resolve differently.
findings.text: §9 says the synthesised keys "take the layer of the `lanes.*` entry they were expanded from", but `_record_provenance` (reckon/flight.py:1152-1164) recurses into mappings and records only leaf paths, so there is no provenance entry at `lanes.claude` or `lanes.claude.models.opus` for an implementer to read; the layer must be taken from a leaf (or from `lanes.claude.*`), and the two differ the moment a project layer overrides a model leaf without the lane

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every anchor resolves: `expand_lanes` (reckon/flight.py:1352), `_lane_entry` (1320), `_apply_catalogue` (1228), `flight_report` (2042), `ResolvedFlight.provenance` (175), `origin()` (180), and `test_default_stdout_parses_as_json_and_exits_zero` (tests/test_flight.py:1356, which does pin the seven-key top-level payload set).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §9's done-when names two tests that must fail on the current resolver plus the existing `origin()` assertions as the standing control; resolving the live flight on 2026-10-08 reproduces the pre-fix state those tests key on (zero provenance under `backends.claude` and `backends.codex`), so the control can be seen to fire.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the write paths are repository paths (`reckon/flight.py`, `tests/test_flight.py`, the section's new test module); no gate log or artifact is directed to a session scratchpad or node-local temporary directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §9 carries no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers, version tags or changelog prose; it names mechanisms (`expand_lanes`, `_apply_catalogue`, `provenance_sources`) rather than tracker entries.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §9's root cause matches its evidence (the expansion records no provenance, so lane-built entries carry none) and the mechanism runs on the real path `resolve()` → `expand_lanes` (reckon/flight.py:1499) → `flight_report` (2063), but the rule it gives for the synthesised keys names a provenance layer that does not exist as a record.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable: per-key provenance (and its companion source-key map) for every entry `expand_lanes` builds, lane-named or derived.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §9 declares no depends-on/informs/gates and needs none: it edits the expansion in `reckon/flight.py` and the flight payload, neither of which is gated by the `every-module-fits-a-worker-window` §4 split that gates §4 and §10.
